15:20 Local Time, 13:20 GMT, 18:50 IST: March 2023 was the last time Australia lost a Test series. They've been a great team under Cummins, winning the WTC in 2023, and then making the final in 2025. But their bowling attack isn't getting any younger, their batting seems to be vulnerable, and they've been beaten by the better team over the last couple of weeks. After a sensational win in Gqeberha to level the series, South Africa have registered yet another remarkable come-from-behind win here in Cape Town. Today it was set up to be a humdinger with Australia needing 288 in the fourth innings, and South Africa needing 10 wickets. There was such excitement about all the posibilities of a close contest. But it turned out to be an anticlimax with the match being decided in the first session thanks to a procession of wickets from Rabada and Harmer.

Quite remarkable how Test cricket has so many life lessons tucked into it. On the opening morning, Pat Cummins' decision to bowl first on a flat deck came under scrutiny as South Africa's batters made the Australian attack look ordinary. Yet, by the end of the day, Australia had turned things around spectacularly, claiming the last four wickets for just two runs. Their batters carried that momentum forward, with five of the top six getting past 40. Josh Inglis, stepping in for the injured Steve Smith, ensured the absence of Australia's premier Test batter wasn't felt, producing a magnificent century. A handy 100-run lead followed, and by the close of Day 3, South Africa were effectively 40/4 in their second innings, with the game firmly in the balance.

Facing a must-win situation on Day 4, the hosts responded in style through magnificent centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder. Their match-defining 154-run stand for the sixth wicket helped South Africa set Australia a daunting target of 288. Both sides would have fancied their chances heading into the final day, but only one managed to turn belief into action. Kagiso Rabada, who had been laid low by illness on Days 2 and 3, returned with a vengeance, striking twice in the opening over before removing Australia's biggest hope, Travis Head, six overs later. From there, Simon Harmer tightened the screws with a web of spin, finishing with a well-deserved maiden ten wicket haul in the game. South Africa eventually stormed to a memorable 176-run victory, clinching the series 2-1 and reclaiming the No. 1 spot in Test cricket. All in all, a terrific series in which both sides fought tooth and nail. Stick around for the post-match reactions!

South Africa, under Bavuma, continue to achieve incredible things. Down 0-1 in the series, they've gone on to produce two great comeback wins in consecutive Tests to take the series along with the No. 1 Test ranking. The trophy is theirs and Bavuma takes it to his teammates as they pose for the photos with the Table Mountain in the backdrop. As for Australia, there has already been a lot of debate over some of the choices that were made this week, including the decision to leave out Scott Boland and particularly the decision to bowl first. A stunning second new ball spell from Mitchell Starc raised hopes of getting them out of jail but it wasn't to be. Their batting remains a major concern and after the exclusion of Nic Maddinson, there are now big question marks about the future of Marnus Labuschagne. Their bowling attack isn't getting any younger either. Will be interesting to see what they do when New Zealand come touring in December.

So that's all from this series which many feel should've been four or five Tests long. But we take what we get, and what we got was a lot of fun. Hope you enjoyed our coverage. It's a goodbye from Sagar Chawla on behalf of Praveen Kumar and Raju Peethala!
